_comment: Tunings for the UWARUco detector in uwaruco.py. Same idea as 01_Calibration/detector_presets.json:
a tuning is a data change, and the preset a run used is written into that run's calibration YAML.
Keys must name a field of uwaruco.Params; a typo fails at load rather than being ignored.
markerBorderBits and errorCorrectionRate are NOT set here. They describe the printed target, not
the tuning, and are read from 01_Calibration/detector_presets.json so that the two detectors
cannot disagree about what is on the board.
'_version' picks which of the paper's two workflows to run, 'base' (Figure 2b) or 'masked'
(Figure 2c). '_feedback' applies to the masked version only: 'self' re-runs each image with a
mask derived from its own first pass, 'sequential' carries the mask from the previous image the
way the paper does for video, and 'none' disables masking entirely.
Measured on every fifth frame of 18_Sep/Rigframes (42 images), usable = at least 10 tags.
The incumbent, aruco 'wide', gets 17/42 usable and 808 tags. See README.md for the full table
and for why the paper's two headline choices go opposite ways on this footage:
paper        adaptiveThreshConstant = 0    15/42 usable,  545 tags   the paper's numbers
tuned        constant = 4, bits from Otsu  22/42 usable,  926 tags   the recommended preset
adaptiveThreshConstant = 0 collapses detection here because these tags are low-contrast rather
than dark, which is the same effect detector_presets.json records for the ArUco detector.
About the window sizes: the paper's 10, 20 and 40 pixels were tuned on 1920x1080 footage. These
frames are 1280x720, two thirds of that in each dimension. Scaling them helps a little; sweeping
the full 3..53 range helps more, because the tags here run from a few pixels across to filling
the frame and three windows cannot cover that.

tuned._why: The paper's workflow with the two settings this footage disagrees with put back: a threshold constant between ARUco's 7 and the paper's 0, bits read by Otsu, and windows swept over the range the tags actually span. Best measured: 22/42 usable, 926 tags.

tuned_mean._why: A tried-and-rejected idea, kept so the result is reproducible: average the corners of the passes that agree instead of keeping the largest quad. Identical detections, but a clearly WORSE calibration (common-subset RMS 3.367/2.503 px against tuned's 2.694/1.727), because the window sizes place the border at different systematic offsets and averaging mixes biases rather than cancelling noise. Do not use; see README.md.

tuned_base._why: The 'tuned' settings without the mask, so the mask's contribution is measurable on its own.

paper._why: The Masked version exactly as published: windows 10/20/40, nothing subtracted from the local mean, bits read from the thresholded image. Kept so the published algorithm can be run unmodified.

paper_base._why: The Base version as published (no mask, no median filter), to show what the mask is worth.

scaled._why: The paper's settings with only the windows scaled from 1920x1080 to this footage's 1280x720: 10/20/40 -> 7/13/27. Isolates the resolution difference from the footage difference.

scaled_otsu._why: Scaled windows and Otsu bits, but the paper's constant of 0. Isolates the bit source from the threshold constant.
